title: The Last Postcard
premise: Edmund Okonkwo inherited a debt-ridden vineyard and a decade-old secret: the woman he loved, Marguerite, vanished after one perfect summer, leaving only an unsigned postcard. When a snowstorm traps her — now engaged to his business rival, wine distributor Callum Reyes — at his farmhouse, the three are forced to confront what really happened the night she left. As thaw comes and the vineyard's first harvest approaches, Edmund must choose between protecting Marguerite's old lie (which shields her family) and claiming the truth that could win her back. He speaks the rehearsed sentence at the harvest festival; she chooses him, not out of nostalgia but because truth finally feels like belonging.
about_author: Astrid Villalobos is a former sommelier who traded restaurant cellars for quiet mornings writing love stories set among vines and weather. She lives in wine country with her partner and an opinionated dog named Vintage.

chapters.title: Five Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Five years after inheriting the bankrupt vineyard, Edmund walks his carefully ordered life: ledgers, pruning schedules, small safe steps. A letter from distributor Callum Reyes promises a contract that could save the estate. Beat: cautious hope shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: The Postcard in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Preparing the guest room for Callum's visit, Edmund finds the unsigned postcard he's kept for a decade — Marguerite's handwriting, no return address. Flashback fragments of their last summer. Beat: grief resurfacing under routine.

chapters.title: The Rival Arrives
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Charming, ambitious Callum tours the struggling vineyard, sizing up both the wine and its guarded owner. He mentions, casually, his fiancée. Beat: wary mutual respect between two men measuring each other.

chapters.title: Snow on the Pass
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite insists on joining Callum's trip, telling herself it's about the wine, not the valley. The storm closes the mountain pass early. Beat: dread disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: All three POV rotation. The storm strands all three at the farmhouse. Marguerite and Edmund see each other for the first time in ten years over a candlelit kitchen. Beat: shock, denial, electricity.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Power fails; they shelter in the cellar among barrels Edmund can't yet afford to fill. Marguerite touches the oak like an old friend. Callum watches them, sensing history. Beat: memory pressing against the present.

chapters.title: Two Truths at Dinner
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. By lantern light, Callum probes their past while performing ease. Marguerite lies smoothly; Edmund refuses to lie but says nothing. Beat: loyalty vs. truth begins its quiet war.

chapters.title: The Night She Left
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Unable to sleep, Marguerite recalls the real reason she fled: her father's crimes, the threat against Edmund's family if she stayed. Beat: guilt crystallizing into resolve to keep silent.

chapters.title: Thaw Water
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Storm breaks; roads clear; Callum extends their stay citing business. Edmund and Marguerite walk the frozen vines alone and almost speak the truth. Beat: longing vs. self-protection.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum offers the distribution deal — contingent on exclusivity and, subtly, on Edmund keeping distance from Marguerite. Beat: temptation wearing a professional face.

chapters.title: Old Letters, New Lies
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite finds Edmund kept every letter she never sent, drafts hidden in the farmhouse walls by her younger self. She burns one. Beat: shame and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Working the vines together, hands brushing, they fall into old rhythm. Edmund nearly says the rehearsed sentence — 'I know why you left' — and stops. Beat: the cost of silence made physical.

chapters.title: Callum Sees It
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum confronts Marguerite privately; she admits nothing, but he knows. His jealousy curdles into strategy: accelerate the engagement announcement. Beat: rival becomes antagonist.

chapters.title: The Engagement Toast
chapters.summary: All three POV. At the village inn, Callum announces their wedding date publicly. Edmund drinks and congratulates them with steady hands. Marguerite watches him choose silence again. Beat: public humiliation as private wound.

chapters.title: Father's Shadow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite's brother arrives with news: their father is dying and wants confession before death — the old threat may be void. Marguerite wavers between freedom and fear. Beat: the lie's foundation cracking.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund finally tells Marguerite he has known for years why she left — her brother confessed once, drunk — and he stayed silent to protect her. Betrayal and relief war on her face. Beat: truth offered without demand.

chapters.title: Vines Don't Wait
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Harvest begins; Callum sabotages the contract talks, threatening the vineyard's survival unless Edmund withdraws gracefully. Edmund refuses to trade Marguerite's name for grapes. Beat: stakes become existential.

chapters.title: Confession at the Hospital
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her dying father confesses everything — the threats, the forged debts that burdened Edmund's inheritance. Marguerite realizes Edmund lost years to her family's sin. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Storm Before Harvest
chapters.summary: All three POV. An early frost threatens the first viable harvest; rivals and lovers work side by side through the night to save the grapes. Callum, exhausted, sees who Marguerite truly is. Beat: crisis stripping pretense away.

chapters.title: The Sentence Spoken
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the harvest festival, before the whole valley, Edmund says the sentence he rehearsed for a decade: 'I have loved you since the summer you left, and I will not apologize for it.' Beat: climax — courage over safety.

chapters.title: Her Answer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite ends the engagement honestly, returns Callum's ring with respect, and chooses Edmund — not the boy from memory, but the man who told the truth. Beat: resolution of loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: First Pour
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Spring again: the first bottled vintage, labeled with a postcard image. Callum, surprisingly, distributes it anyway. Edmund mails a signed postcard to no address — gratitude, not longing. Beat: belonging found; memory honored, released.
